research.summary: Gavin Andresen publicly announced the launch of the Bitcoin Foundation on 27 September 2012.
research.significance: It was an early attempt to standardize, protect and promote Bitcoin through an organized nonprofit body.

research.summary: Coinbase states that it was founded in June 2012.
research.significance: Coinbase became one of the most consequential regulated fiat on-ramps and later the first major US crypto exchange to list publicly.

research.summary: The XRP Ledger first launched in June 2012 after development by David Schwartz, Jed McCaleb and Arthur Britto.
research.significance: XRPL was an early major alternative to proof-of-work cryptocurrencies and focused on fast payments and settlement.

research.summary: Bitcoin Savings & Trust ceased operating after a scheme that the SEC later proved had offered Bitcoin-denominated investments from February 2011 through August 2012.
research.significance: The collapse became the first major Bitcoin-denominated Ponzi case to produce landmark US securities enforcement.

events.title: ASIC Bitcoin mining begins to emerge

research.summary: 2012 saw public ASIC projects and preorders, including ASICMINER's August project announcement; large-scale shipping hardware followed later.
research.significance: The year marks the transition from GPU/FPGA mining toward application-specific mining hardware, but 'ASIC mining begins' should be treated as a period, not one day.

events.title: Bitcoinica collapse highlights early exchange counterparty risk

research.summary: Bitcoinica suffered multiple security incidents in 2012. A May breach alone drained 18,547 BTC after production servers were compromised, following an earlier March cloud-host compromise.
research.significance: Bitcoinica became an early warning about exchange leverage, hot-wallet security and counterparty risk.

events.title: Bitcoin Foundation forms around protocol advocacy and standardization

research.summary: This is the same Bitcoin Foundation launch as LORE-EVT-0078.

events.title: Coinbase starts buying and selling Bitcoin for US customers

research.summary: Coinbase began building a simple consumer on-ramp for buying, holding and selling Bitcoin after its June 2012 founding.
research.significance: This is product/adoption context rather than a separately verified launch date in the current evidence set.

events.title: Ripple consensus ledger launches without proof-of-work mining

research.summary: This row describes the XRP Ledger's non-proof-of-work consensus architecture at launch.
research.significance: Keep as technical context under the canonical XRPL launch.

events.title: Butterfly Labs and ASIC preorders become mining-industry lore

research.summary: Butterfly Labs and other vendors took ASIC-era preorders before dependable mass delivery, generating both excitement and controversy.
research.significance: Useful mining-industry lore, but exact product-preorder claims need vendor-specific source work before a card.

events.title: ASICMiner emerges as a major early Bitcoin ASIC operation

research.summary: ASICMINER publicly announced its investor-backed project to design and operate Bitcoin ASIC mining chips on 9 August 2012.
research.significance: ASICMINER was one of the earliest visible attempts to industrialize purpose-built Bitcoin mining silicon.

events.title: SatoshiDice becomes a major on-chain gambling application

research.summary: SatoshiDICE was announced on BitcoinTalk on 24 April 2012 and rapidly became one of Bitcoin's largest sources of on-chain transactions.
research.significance: It demonstrated borderless on-chain gambling, provable fairness and the first major debate over application-generated transaction 'spam.'

research.summary: Vitalik Buterin and Mihai Alisie co-founded Bitcoin Magazine; its first issue was published in May 2012, not 2013.
research.significance: Bitcoin Magazine placed Buterin at the center of early crypto journalism before he conceived Ethereum.

events.title: Peercoin introduces coin-age concepts in proof-of-stake design

research.summary: Peercoin's blockchain started on 19 August 2012, after an announcement nine days earlier, using a hybrid proof-of-work/proof-of-stake design.
research.significance: Peercoin was an early major proof-of-stake experiment and influenced later consensus-system design.

research.summary: Bitcoin's block subsidy fell from 50 BTC to 25 BTC at block 210,000 on 28 November 2012.
research.significance: The first halving proved Bitcoin's programmed monetary schedule would execute in practice and established a four-year market ritual.
